title: NB Harness Pack Manifest
description: The contract every NB Pack ships as nb-pack.json. A pack extends NB into a domain (product, frontend, testing, ...) but stays SUBORDINATE to Core: it must declare which Core rules it rides on, which workflows it adds, what artifacts it produces, what evidence is required, which review gate applies, how it updates .nb/state, and how it feeds the Harness Score. If a pack's work cannot be recorded, reviewed, and briefed, it does not belong in NB. scripts/validate-packs.mjs enforces these rules dependency-free.

id.description: Pack identifier. MUST match the folder name under packs/ (e.g. packs/product -> id 'product').

description.description: One line: the domain capability this pack adds and the Core discipline it leans on.

domain.description: Domain this pack covers (e.g. product, frontend, testing). Free-form but should be a single word.

status.description: Maturity marker. 'scaffold' = manifest + docs prove the architecture, behavior not yet implemented. 'experimental' = some declared additions ship and run but the contract may still change. 'stable' = additions ship and the contract is settled. Sample packs are scaffolds; do not claim 'experimental'/'stable' without shipping the declared additions.

requires_core.description: Core control rules this pack depends on (snake_case ids). Every pack MUST include intent_lock, evidence_ledger, review_gate, and harness_score — a pack that does not ride those four is not subordinate to Core and is rejected. Packs should also pass through human_brief: every pack's work ends in a plain-language brief.

adds_agents.description: Pack-scoped agent names this pack adds (or WILL add — for scaffolds these are declared intent, not shipped files). Pack agents are namespaced under the pack, never new root agents.

adds_skills.description: Pack-scoped skill names this pack adds (declared intent for scaffolds). A pack skill must create automatic intervention not already covered by Core.

adds_workflows.description: Workflows this pack adds or extends. Pack workflows still run the Core gates; they only change the task flow for the domain.

produces_artifacts.description: Artifact-ledger types this pack writes to .nb/. Must use the Core artifact vocabulary — a pack does not invent its own artifact types.

evidence_required.description: What evidence must exist before this pack's work can be claimed done (e.g. 'VERIFY_CMD output', 'before/after screenshot'). Non-empty: a pack with no required evidence cannot be briefed honestly.

review_gate.description: The review gate this pack applies. cross_family is NB's default (two different model families). cross_family_plus_human stacks a human sign-off (e.g. taste check) on top. human_required means a human must approve before done.

approvals_required.description: User approvals this pack may require before it proceeds (e.g. 'scope change beyond definition_of_done', 'visual sign-off'). May be empty.

state_updates.description: .nb/state.json fields this pack reads or writes (e.g. definition_of_done, taste_notes, last_evidence). Keeps the State Machine the single source of truth — a pack does not keep hidden state.

dimensions.description: Which Harness Score dimensions this pack feeds. A pack cannot move the score by inventing a new dimension; it strengthens existing ones.

note.description: How the pack tightens those dimensions.

harness_score_contribution.description: How this pack contributes to the Harness Score. The score stays Core-owned; the pack only feeds known dimensions.

install_deps.description: Dependencies the pack needs. If non-empty, Core's Install Safety flow applies: show plan -> user approves -> pin version -> prefer local.

permissions.description: Capabilities the pack requests. Same vocabulary as a module manifest, so risk stays explicit to AI and human.

safety_gates.description: Which Core safety/control gates apply to this pack's work. A pack can only request from the Core gate set — it cannot weaken or bypass the safety floor.

exit_criteria.description: What marks this pack's work complete and ready to claim done. Non-empty: a pack that cannot say when it is finished does not belong in NB.

close_contract.description: The machine-readable contract /nb:close enforces for this pack (the SOT; evidence_required is the human-readable derivative). FLAT shape, matching what scripts/lib/close-engine.mjs + scripts/close.mjs actually read. Optional for scaffold/experimental packs; REQUIRED for status:stable (scripts/validate-packs.mjs enforces that, and that a stable contract carries at least one proof OR an explicit floor_only flag). Subjective/taste gates are NOT here — they ride the Core category-floor decision path; analytical proofs cover reasoning/review claims.

activation_rules.description: How /nb:close OBSERVES this pack as active (beyond an explicit declaration): match hook-logged file paths / commands (+ git diff). Each rule is a SUBSTRING matcher by default; a string delimited like /pattern/flags is compiled to a RegExp at load (validator checks it compiles). The AI can add a pack, never remove one — activation is recomputed at close.

objective_proofs.description: Machine-verifiable proofs: a command that ran (reconciled against the hook tool-event log). Verified by verifyProof.

proof_type.description: Unique within the pack (across objective+analytical). No dots — evidence_ref:proof:<pack>.<type> uses '.' as the pack/type separator.

strength.description: Required iff effective strength (max of task strength and category floor) >= this.

command_match.description: Optional. The command this proof_type must have run, as a substring or /pattern/flags regex. /nb:close (verifyProof) REJECTS a proof whose recorded command does not match — this binds proof_type to its real check so an unrelated exit-0 command (e.g. `npm test` labeled `migration-down`) cannot satisfy it. Omit for proofs whose command is inherently project-specific (e.g. testing `verify`).

required_when_workflow.description: Optional. Makes this proof OPT-IN: required at close only when state.current_workflow equals this value. Absent => always required.

analytical_proofs.description: Two kinds, dispatched by proof_type: (1) cross-review COVERAGE proofs — a hash-bound cross-family review whose covers_claims resolve to verified evidence (verifyAnalytical), declared with required_claims; (2) LOG-PAIR proofs (tdd-red-green) — a command pair reconciled against the tool log (verifyTddRedGreen), declared with command_match instead of required_claims.

required_when_workflow.description: Optional. Makes this proof OPT-IN: required at close only when state.current_workflow equals this value (e.g. tdd-red-green only under the `tdd` workflow). Absent => always required.

command_match.description: LOG-PAIR proofs only (tdd-red-green): the test command its red/green runs must match (substring or /pattern/flags). Invalid on coverage proofs.

items.description: Coverage proofs only: claim_id the analytical proof must cover. Unique within the pack. No dots. (Omit for log-pair proofs.)

floor_only.description: A status:stable pack that legitimately ships with NO proof and relies solely on the Core category floor. Must be paired with floor_only_reason. Without this flag, a stable pack with no proofs is invalid.

floor_only_reason.description: Why this stable pack needs no objective/analytical proof (category-floor decision is sufficient).
